topic: Roadways and National Highways of Geography
description: The Indian road network is one of the largest in the world. It is crucial for the transportation of goods and passengers, and is broadly classified into National Highways, State Highways, District Roads, and Rural Roads.

sections.title: Classification of Roads
sections.description: The primary classification of Indian roads based on their construction and maintenance responsibilities.

key_concepts.explanation: These are the primary road networks connecting state capitals, major ports, and railway junctions. They are constructed and maintained by the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
These roads connect the state capital with various district headquarters. Their construction and maintenance are handled by the State Public Works Department (PWD).
Roads of strategic importance in the northern and north-eastern border areas of the country. They are constructed and maintained by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).

sections.title: Important Organizations and Projects
sections.description: Major institutions and government schemes related to road development and management in India.

historical_events.significance: Formed for the rapid development and maintenance of road networks in border areas to provide logistical support to the armed forces.
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) became operational as an autonomous agency for the development, maintenance, and management of National Highways (under the NHAI Act, 1988).
A nationwide scheme launched to provide all-weather road connectivity to unconnected villages across the country.

An umbrella program for the highways sector that focuses on optimizing the efficiency of freight and passenger movement by bridging critical infrastructure gaps through economic corridors and border connectivity.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Frequently asked one-liner facts related to road transport in India.

important_facts.fact: Maharashtra ranks first in India in terms of the total length of the road network.
National Highways constitute only about 2% of the total road network in India, but they carry nearly 40% of the total road traffic.
Kerala is one of the leading states in India in terms of road density (length of road per 100 sq. km of area).
Atal Tunnel (9.02 km), built under the Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh, is the longest highway tunnel in the world at an altitude of over 10,000 feet.
